According to the Circular of National Development and Reform Commission on Approval of Establishing Pilot Area for National Urban-rural Integration Reform in Chongqing and Chengdu issued on June 7, 2007, Chongqing was approved as the pilot area for national urban-rural integration reform.

The State Council requests Chongqing to accelerate the urban and rural integration development and reform to set an example for the whole nation.

This is a significant strategic deployment of the country to boost development of the Middle and West China and also an important measure to implement scientific outlook on development and to promote development of a harmonious society.

Chongqing is a combination of both large urban and rural areas.

Chongqing has complex landform, varied geomorphic and abundant resources.
It is the major grain production area and the production base of commodity pork.

The rural area covers a large area, agriculture takes a large proportion and there are still lots of surplus rural labor there.
There is large gap of income distribution and development stage between urban and rural areas and among different areas.

Benzun Monastery has a long-standing reputation in Yongchuan and surrounding districts and counties.
Chongqing Huayan Monastery and this monastery are the sister monasteries since their elders are of the same seniority mark and from the same Buddhist division.

The three large halls of Benzun Monastery, Tianwang Hall, Guanyin Hall and Daxiong Hall, the three small halls, Yong’an Hall, Chenghuang Hall and Manjusri Samantabhadra Hall, Shiwang Hall and Bell & Drum Pavilion no longer exist due to historical reasons, and several Buddha statues (Fig. 2) are kept only in some rooms of Benzun Monastery (Fig. 1), and some believers have built, at their own cost, another two small halls (Fig. 3) at this historic site.
The morning chimes and evening prayer are occasionally heard in Benzun Monastery and the pilgrims are much less now than in the period when it was flourishing.

However, thanks to its long-lasting culture of Buddhist, some non-governmental organizations, including “Fuyuan Association” and “Jixian Association”, will organize the believers together on the birthday of Guanyin (February 19 in Chinese calendar) and on the Gala of Buddha (April 8 in Chinese calendar).
They will carry the Buddha’s seat, wave colored flags and sing “Namo Amitabha”.
The believers may pray for happiness, longevity, wealth or descendants, or confess a sin.
In addition, various retailers and the flourishing amusement and service industries here make the festival jollier.
Benzun Monastery, a historically valuable site, is classified as Yongchuan’s district-level cultural heritage.
Chongqing Yongchuan People’s Government and Banqiao Town have planned to rebuild Benzun Monastery when appropriate to pass down the Buddhist culture and build a harmonious society.
Summary of Environmental Impact Assessment Report for CURIP 322 The clay-bound road in Fig. 3 and Fig. 4 is the existing Benzun Monastery section of No. 2 road.

It is planned, before the site investigation by the CPMO and EIA experts, to expand this road and thus form the Benzun Monastery section of No. 2 road in sub-component of road infrastructure project in Banqiao Town of Yongchuan City, which will occupy the land owned by this monastery.
Moreover, the existing Benzun Monastery section road leads to the newly built monastery gate and is along the central axis of some halls of Benzun Monastery.
It follows that the expansion of this section will damage the traditional integrality of this monastery and cause serious religious disputes.

Benzun Villagers, the Buddhist believers and Mr. Li, head of Yongchuan County Administration of Cultural Heritage, all supported the expansion and reconstruction of No. 2 Road during the investigation.
They said that there were always traffic jams and large crowd once there were important Buddhist activities or on holidays and the expansion of road will make their life and work more convenient.

Believers and tourists from the regions hundreds miles away can pass down such Buddhist culture as peace, luck, kin dness, “Tolerance brings respect”, “Cause breeds effect” etc. via exchange of religious culture to obtain soul inspiration.

A head of Yongchuan County Administration of Ethnic and Religious Affairs emphasized that the planned restoration and reconstruction of Benzun Monastery must be taken into consideration during construction of road.
The head also said they should abide by all the religious traditions in respect of Chinese Buddhist monasteries.
The expansion of existing road will cause the road to cross the monastery and to occupy the new gate and central axis of several halls, which is a great taboo for Buddhist monasteries.

Fan, a member of the team of establishing Buddhist site in Benzun Monastery, also requested the experts and the PIU to consider the possible response of believers if the road occupies the land for the monastery.

Through investigation, the CPMO and EIA experts strongly recommended the PIU to choose another route for Benzun Monastery section of No. 2 road, i.e. to detour Benzun Monastery to the east of this monastery.
This is consistent with the World Bank’s comprehensive policies on cultural heritage.

The World Bank will help protect cultural heritage and avoid damages in the projects funded by it; it will provide Summary of Environmental Impact Assessment Report for CURIP 323 protection and improvement for the cultural heritage involved instead of just leaving it as it is now.
It is advised to choose another route for the project on certain conditions to protect, study on and restore the sites and buildings.
The sub-component PIU also recognized, via investigation, the problems of the former route selected.
It agreed to adopt the alternative to detour Benzun Monastery and to modify relevant documents as soon as possible.
Benzun Monastery is an ancient cultural heritage with great historic values.
The tablet (Fig. 5) excavated by believers from ruins indicates that Benzun Monastery is of significant importance for the study on Buddhist culture and on local culture and history.

The contractor of this section shall prepare and submit detailed construction plan for protecting cultural heritage as one of the construction organization proposals, and abide by the same during management and supervision of construction.
